title: Planar Poisson Limit of Optimal Lipschitz Balancing Weights with Two Covariates

gap_reasons: The exact frontier concerns normalized outcome-linear estimation of a conditional sample contrast under uniform planar covariates, fair randomization and known unit Gaussian noise; observational designs and nonlinear-estimator optimality remain outside the delivered result.
The interior coordinates are characterized through an attained stationary variational problem and terminating enclosures, without quantitative endpoint rates or a finite-sample approximation rate.
The certification argument guarantees eventual termination but supplies no tractable complexity guarantee, limiting immediate numerical usefulness.
tldr: For randomized Gaussian outcomes with two uniform continuous covariates, the full Euclidean Lipschitz class has a unique conditional-design RMSE optimum among all normalized outcome-linear estimators, equal to the specified sign-constrained optimizer. Its separate scaled variance and worst-bias coordinates converge to the unique attained stationary planar Poisson transport optimum at every public \(c>0\). Convergent unconditional finite-square programs and an adaptive algorithm certify risk and both coordinates to every requested positive accuracy, with proved termination. Fractional constant-load obstruction and guarded local reallocation give strict separation from both endpoints and exclude a finite matching plateau. Exact conditional Gaussian coverage is inherited, and the new coordinates determine interval length uniformly on compact positive radius intervals. A worked \(c=1,\eta=1/100\) execution is optional future numerical work and has not been reported.
gap: Finite Lipschitz transport optimization is published, as are regular-regime weighting limits and fixed-match variance geometry. The inspected results do not identify both coordinates of this fixed-radius planar endogenous-load optimizer or certify them numerically.
